evidence_class: fixed kernel source analysis plus a preserved generic-VM log observation

failure_indicators.condition: positive count; audit/kauditd, or conservative broader kernel scope

findings.conclusion: The retained v7 raw log contains a positive shared-printk suppression warning; missing content is unknown.
kauditd prints non-EOE records through the shared printk_ratelimit state.
The false printk branch does not call audit_log_lost; this is distinct from audit_lost and from deliberate EOE exclusion.
Nonzero interval permits an uncounted try-lock rejection; no suppression line alone is not completeness proof.
The zero interval path returns true before the state lock and quota. Burst zero is not the same operation.
Registered scalar interval is ASCII seconds using proc_dointvec_jiffies; zero writes the shared interval as zero. Burst uses a different scalar handler.
Audit rate, backlog, retry/hold queues and allocation failure loss are separate and remain unchanged.
Shared printk interval does not disable separate local ratelimit states or the userspace devkmsg limiter.

limitations: Interval zero affects future use of one shared printk state only; no old records are recovered.
It does not disable independent per-call-site limiters.
It does not change audit_rate_limit, audit backlog, retry/hold queues, audit rules, failure mode, or Enforcing.
The shared suppression caller label does not identify each omitted record.
No suppression/loss line is not by itself proof that all audit events reached retained serial.
New helper compilation, actual parameter values, setting readback and complete runtime gates require subsequent separate evidence.
No TB371FC native-Linux or Android hardware support is established.
